title: Just a little more
situation: Your demo trade on USD/JPY is 45 pips in profit and close to your [[take-profit|take profit]] at 50 pips. It looks strong. You start imagining it running 150 pips and want to remove the target.
question: What do you do next?

responses.text: Remove the take profit and the [[stop-loss|stop loss]] so nothing gets in the way.
responses.explanation: With no stop, nothing limits how much of the gain, or more, you can give back.

responses.text: Leave the target where your plan put it. If you want to test a different exit, write it down and try it on future trades.
responses.explanation: Exits chosen before the trade are part of what you are testing. A new idea can be tested properly, not on a feeling mid-trade.

responses.text: Close half at your target and let the rest run with the stop moved to your entry price.
responses.explanation: A plan can include this kind of exit on purpose. Decided mid-trade on a feeling, though, it is not your plan, and you cannot tell if it helps.

takeaway: Exits are decided before the trade, when you are calm. Change them in review, not in the moment.
